content.title: Duke men's basketball defeats Siena in 2026 NCAA Tournament first round game
content.text: Skip to content by: Hannah Leyva Posted: Mar 19, 2026 / 05:05 PM EDT Updated: Mar 19, 2026 / 06:49 PM EDT SHARE GREENVILLE, S.C. (WNCN) — Right out of the gate, the Duke Blue Devils, the No. 1 overall team in the NCAA Tournament, looked flat in their first round game Thursday afternoon. No. 16 Siena could sense it and jumped all over them, leading 43-32 at halftime. But the Blue Devils (33-2) came back in the second half, using two scoring runs to eventually complete the comeback and take the game, 71-65, over the Saints (23-12) in the East region matchup. Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year Cameron Boozer scored 22 points and pulled down 13 rebounds for Duke, while twin brother Cayden Boozer added 19 points and 5 assists. Isaiah Evans also notched a double-double with 16 points and 10 rebounds. Siena, coached by former Syracuse player Gerry McNamara, did not use any substitutions until the last minute, playing all five starters nearly the whole 40 minutes. Gavin Doty led the way for the Saints with a game-high 21 points. Freshman forward Francis Folefac added 18 points and seven rebounds for Siena. Duke now moves on to play TCU in a second round game Saturday.
